question: Should OpenClaw standardize a `tools.fs` allow/deny policy for filesystem tools while explicitly excluding arbitrary `exec`, or require a stronger sandbox/account boundary before presenting this as host filesystem protection?
rationale: Path parsing cannot reliably make unrestricted shell execution equivalent to a filesystem authorization boundary, while a new public config contract affects existing tool behavior, setup guidance, and operator threat assumptions.

options.title: Define file-tool scope first
options.body: Adopt a clearly named `tools.fs` normalized allow/deny contract for file and local-media tools, state that it does not authorize or sandbox arbitrary shell commands, and direct stronger isolation to sandbox backends.

options.title: Require an end-to-end boundary
options.body: Defer the configuration surface until OpenClaw can pair it with a supported OS/container/account execution boundary that also contains shell-mediated access.

options.title: Keep workspace-only only
options.body: Retain the current workspace-only guard and close the broader policy direction only if maintainers intentionally reject granular host-path configuration.

recommendation.title: Define file-tool scope first
recommendation.body: Adopt a clearly named `tools.fs` normalized allow/deny contract for file and local-media tools, state that it does not authorize or sandbox arbitrary shell commands, and direct stronger isolation to sandbox backends.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied maintainer review already framed the unresolved tool-policy and exec boundary, and the current workspace-only lineage is associated with this area.
